help: Create a sandbox.

fields.help: Optional sandbox name (auto-generated when omitted).
Create the sandbox from a named sandbox template.

Sandbox source: a rootfs tar archive (`.tar`, `.tar.gz`, or `.tgz`) or a container image reference (e.g., `myregistry.com/img:tag`).  To use a local Dockerfile, build and tag it with the container engine used by your local gateway, then pass the resulting image reference here. A rootfs tar is staged for the VM compute driver.

Upload local files into the sandbox before running.  Format: `<LOCAL_PATH>[:<SANDBOX_PATH>]`. When `SANDBOX_PATH` is omitted, files are uploaded to the container's working directory. Inside a Git work tree, `.gitignore` rules are applied by default. Outside a Git work tree, uploads proceed unfiltered with a warning. Filtering errors or empty selections stop the upload; use `--no-git-ignore` to intentionally upload everything.  Cannot be combined with a trailing command, because uploads finish after the main process starts. Create the sandbox without a command, then run the workload with `sandbox exec`.
Disable `.gitignore` filtering for `--upload`.
Deprecated compatibility flag. Sandboxes are kept by default.
Delete the sandbox after the initial command or shell exits.
Launch a remote editor after the sandbox is ready. Keeps the sandbox alive and installs OpenShell-managed SSH config.
Request GPU resources for the sandbox.  Omit COUNT for the driver's default GPU selection, or pass COUNT to request a specific number of GPUs.
CPU limit for the sandbox (for example: 500m, 1, 2.5).
Memory limit for the sandbox (for example: 512Mi, 4Gi, 8G).

Driver-keyed JSON object for driver-specific sandbox settings. Disabled unless the gateway administrator enables `allow_driver_config`. External resource attachments still require approval labels.  For Kubernetes, pass a value such as `{"kubernetes":{"pod":{"node_selector":{"pool":"gpu"}}}}`.
Attach a configured credential provider to the sandbox. Use providers for API keys, tokens, and other secrets so commands in the sandbox do not receive the real credential values. Repeatable.
Path to a custom sandbox policy YAML file. Overrides the built-in default and the `OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_POLICY` env var.
Forward a local port to the sandbox before the initial command or shell starts. Accepts [`bind_address`:]port (e.g. 8080, 0.0.0.0:8080). Keeps the sandbox alive.
Expose a loopback HTTP or WebSocket service after the sandbox is ready. Keeps the sandbox alive. Use `openshell service expose` to add a named service.
Handling for an incoming application Authorization header.

Allocate a pseudo-terminal for the remote command. Defaults to auto-detection (on when stdin and stdout are terminals). Use --tty to force a PTY even when auto-detection fails, or --no-tty to disable.
Disable pseudo-terminal allocation.
Start the canonical main process without attaching to it.
Restart behavior after the canonical main process exits.
Auto-create missing providers from local credentials.  Without this flag, an interactive prompt asks per-provider; in non-interactive mode the command errors.
Never auto-create providers; error if required providers are missing.
Attach labels to the sandbox (key=value format, repeatable).
Attach non-secret annotations to the sandbox (key=value format, repeatable). Values may contain `/`, spaces, and `=`.

Set a non-secret environment variable in the sandbox. Do not use this option for API keys, tokens, or other secrets; create a provider and attach it with `--provider` instead. Repeatable. Each value is limited to 8 KiB and cannot contain a newline.

Set a sandbox environment variable from the CLI process environment.  Format: `KEY[=ENVVAR]`. When `ENVVAR` is omitted, `KEY` is used. The value does not appear in the CLI process arguments. Repeatable.
Suppress warnings when --env values look like credentials.

Approval mode for agent-authored policy proposals.  `manual` (default): every proposal lands in the draft inbox for human review, regardless of the prover verdict.  `auto`: proposals whose prover delta is empty are approved automatically; proposals with findings still require human approval. Auto mode is an explicit opt-in — `OpenShell`'s default-deny posture is preserved unless you choose otherwise.
Output format.
Command to run after "--" (defaults to an interactive shell). Each argument is limited to 32 KiB.

help: Execute a command in a running sandbox.  Runs a command inside an existing sandbox using the gRPC exec endpoint. Output is streamed to the terminal in real-time. Examples: openshell sandbox exec my-sandbox -- ls -la /workspace openshell sandbox exec --name my-sandbox -- ls -la /workspace openshell sandbox exec -n my-sandbox --workdir /app -- python script.py echo "hello" | openshell sandbox exec -n my-sandbox -- cat

help: Add an existing gateway.  Registers a gateway endpoint so it appears in `openshell gateway select`.  An `http://...` endpoint is treated as a direct plaintext gateway and skips both mTLS client certificate lookup and browser authentication.  Without extra flags, an `https://...` endpoint is treated as an edge-authenticated (cloud) gateway and a browser is opened for authentication.  Pass `--remote <ssh-dest>` to register a remote mTLS gateway. Pass `--local` to register a local mTLS gateway. In both cases, mTLS certificates must already exist in the gateway config directory.  An `ssh://` endpoint (e.g., `ssh://user@host:8080`) is shorthand for `--remote user@host` with the endpoint derived from the URL.

fields.help: Gateway endpoint URL (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, `https://10.0.0.5:8080`, or `ssh://user@host:8080`).
Gateway name (auto-derived from the endpoint hostname when omitted).
Register a remote mTLS gateway accessible via SSH. With `http://...`, stores a remote plaintext registration instead.
Register a local mTLS gateway running in Docker on this machine. With `http://...`, stores a local plaintext registration instead.
Register as an OIDC-authenticated gateway using the given issuer URL. The server must be configured with `--oidc-issuer` matching this URL.
OIDC client ID for the CLI login flow (defaults to "openshell-cli").
OIDC audience for the API resource server. When different from the client ID, the CLI requests this audience in the token exchange. Defaults to the client ID value.
Space-separated `OAuth2` scopes to request during OIDC login. When set, tokens will include these scopes for fine-grained access control.
